knowledge:
- key_parameters: DEGpath=File path to the DEG list of interest (CSV or TSV) ;; genename=Name of the column containing HUGO gene names ;; sampsize=Sample size of the DEG analysis ;; iters=Number of resampling iterations for bootstrapping (default 100,000; can use 50,000 for speed) ;; headers=Character vector defining column names for log fold change and adjusted p-value (default assumes DESeq2 "log2FoldChange" and "padj") ;; scorelist=Output of pathwayAnalysis() or a list of such outputs ;; labeltext=Indication of which values to use to label points in bubblePlot ("Pval" or "LogFC") ;; labelsize=Numeric value for point label text size in bubblePlot (default = 0.25) ;; samplenames=Character vector of names for labeling each output in metaHeatmap ;; pvalcut=P-value cutoff for metaHeatmap (default = 0.05) ;; pathway=Name of the WikiPathway to be plotted in cytoPath ;; figpath=File path where the Cytoscape figure will be saved.
- alternatives: Upstream differential expression analysis packages like DESeq2 or limma are used to generate the input DEG list. RCy3 is used internally by cytoPath to interface with Cytoscape.
- when_to_use: Use when you have a list of differentially expressed genes (DEGs) with fold changes and p-values from RNA-seq or microarray data and want to assess, score, and visualize metabolic pathway dysregulation.
- pitfalls: A seed MUST be set before running pathwayAnalysis() to ensure reproducible bootstrapping results, and it must remain the same throughout the analysis ;; metaHeatmap() cannot be produced if there are no pathways significantly dysregulated below the specified p-value cutoff (pvalcut) ;; metaHeatmap() is only useful when comparing multiple DEG lists/groups and will not work for a single DEG list ;; cytoPath() requires a local instance of Cytoscape running and the RCy3 package installed to render the plot.

workflows.name: single_deg_metabolic_profiling
workflows.intent: Assess metabolic dysregulation from a single DEG list and visualize the profile using a bubble plot.
input: BRCA_DEGS.csv (DEG list containing HUGO gene names, log fold change, and adjusted p-values)
workflows.stages: 1. Set seed for reproducible bootstrapping ;; 2. Run pathway analysis using pathwayAnalysis() ;; 3. Visualize the metabolic profile using bubblePlot() ;; 4. Plot the bubble plot using plot()
workflows.code:
set.seed(1234)

brca <- pathwayAnalysis(DEGpath = system.file("extdata/BRCA_DEGS.csv",
                        package = "MetaPhOR"),
                        genename = "X",
                        sampsize = 1095,
                        iters = 50000,
                        headers = c("logFC", "adj.P.Val"))

pval <- bubblePlot(scorelist = brca,
                    labeltext = "Pval",
                    labelsize = .85)
plot(pval)

logfc <- bubblePlot(scorelist = brca,
                    labeltext = "LogFC",
                    labelsize = .85)
plot(logfc)

workflows.name: multi_deg_comparative_profiling
workflows.intent: Compare metabolic profiles across multiple groups or conditions using a heatmap.
workflows.stages: 1. Run pathway analysis for each condition using pathwayAnalysis() ;; 2. Load pre-calculated scores for comparison conditions ;; 3. Combine the scores into a list ;; 4. Generate a comparative heatmap using metaHeatmap()
workflows.code:
ovca <- read.csv(system.file("extdata/OVCA_Scores.csv", package = "MetaPhOR"),
                header = TRUE,
                row.names = 1)
prad <- read.csv(system.file("extdata/PRAD_Scores.csv", package = "MetaPhOR"),
                header = TRUE,
                row.names = 1)

all.scores <- list(brca, ovca, prad)
names <- c("BRCA", "OVCA", "PRAD")

metaHeatmap(scorelist = all.scores,
            samplenames = names,
            pvalcut = 0.05)

workflows.name: pathway_network_modeling
workflows.intent: Model individual metabolic pathways using transcriptional changes of individual genes and visualize them in Cytoscape.
input: BRCA_DEGS.csv (DEG list containing HUGO gene names, log fold change, and adjusted p-values)
workflows.stages: 1. Identify a pathway of interest ;; 2. Render and save the pathway model using cytoPath() (requires a running local Cytoscape instance)
workflows.code:
cytoPath(pathway = "Tryptophan Metabolism",
            DEGpath = "BRCA_DEGS.csv",
            figpath = paste(getwd(), "BRCA_Tryptophan_Pathway", sep = "/"),
            genename = "X",
            headers = c("logFC", "adj.P.Val"))
